zh.title: 忠實航空十年機隊轉向：從波音到空中巴士、再重返波音
zh.summary: 忠實航空曾靠低價二手MD-80起家，2018年轉為全空中巴士機隊；隨著二手飛機維修成本上升，2022年回頭訂購50架全新波音737MAX，機隊策略再度轉向。
body: 忠實航空1998年以麥道DC-9起家，機隊以MD-80系列為主力，最多擁有61架，其中48架為MD-83型，多為1980年代中期至晚期出廠、曾在北歐航空、大韓航空與墨西哥航空服役的二手飛機。低價購入老飛機、連結美國小城市與拉斯維加斯、奧蘭多等度假勝地的模式，讓機隊持有成本成為獲利關鍵；航空公司也曾引進6架波音757-200投入夏威夷等長程休閒航線，後因不符核心航網而退役。

MD-80油耗高、機齡漸長、維修成本上升，加上接連的機械故障損害聲譽，促使忠實航空自2012年起購入曾服役於易捷航空與伊比利亞航空的二手空中巴士A319與A320。根據2019年1月投資人簡報，A319與A320的油耗比MD-80低約25%至30%，可靠度更高，所需備用機也更少；2018年11月最後一班MD-80客運航班飛完後，忠實航空成為全空中巴士機隊營運商，管理層估計機隊轉型每年可帶來約7500萬美元額外收益。

然而二手A320ceo機齡漸長、維修需求增加，加上737MAX停飛與疫情造成的交付延誤，改變了算盤。2022年1月5日，忠實航空宣布訂購50架全新波音737MAX，包括30架737-7與20架737-8-200，另有50架選擇權；波音預估新機油耗比現有機隊低約20%。訂單其後多次調整：2023年9月修訂增加6架737-8-200、選擇權增至80架；2026年10月再行使6架選擇權，確定訂單增至56架。截至2026年9月30日，合併陽光之鄉航空後的集團共有76架A320、27架A319、21架737MAX8-200、43架737-800與3架737-900ER，737MAX在第三季已占可用座位里程的22%，高於一年前的12%。

en.title: Why Allegiant Air broke with Boeing for an all-Airbus fleet, then came back
en.summary: Allegiant built its business on cheap secondhand Boeing-lineage jets, switched to an all-Airbus fleet in 2018, then returned to Boeing with a 50-aircraft 737 MAX order in 2022 as the economics of used aircraft changed.
body: Allegiant Air began operations in 1998 with McDonnell Douglas DC-9 aircraft and built its fleet around the larger MD-80 family, which became part of Boeing's portfolio after the 1997 merger with McDonnell Douglas. Its historical MD-80 fleet numbered 61 aircraft, 48 of them the MD-83 variant, almost all built in the mid-to-late 1980s and previously flown by airlines such as SAS, Korean Air and Aeromexico. Cheap secondhand jets suited a leisure model built on connecting smaller American cities with vacation destinations such as Las Vegas, Orlando and Florida's Gulf Coast, where aircraft often spent more time on the ground and low ownership costs mattered most. Allegiant also flew six Boeing 757-200s on longer leisure routes, including services to Hawaii, before withdrawing them to concentrate on a simpler fleet.

The MD-80s' high fuel consumption, advancing age, rising maintenance costs and a series of reputation-damaging mechanical incidents eventually forced a fleet overhaul, and Allegiant began acquiring secondhand Airbus A319s and A320s from 2012. According to its January 2019 investor presentation, the Airbus jets consumed approximately 25-30% less fuel than the MD-80 while offering improved reliability and requiring fewer spare aircraft. The transformation culminated in November 2018, when Allegiant operated its final MD-80 passenger flight after 16 years of service, becoming an all-Airbus operator. Management estimated the fleet transformation would generate approximately $75 million in additional annualized earnings.

The economics then shifted again. The Boeing 737 MAX grounding and pandemic-related manufacturing disruption delayed deliveries and pushed airlines to retain older narrowbodies, while Allegiant's secondhand A320ceos aged and maintenance requirements grew. On January 5, 2022, the airline announced an order for 50 Boeing 737 MAX aircraft, split between 30 737-7s and 20 higher-capacity 737-8-200s, with options for another 50, Boeing's first direct order from a US ultra-low-cost carrier. Then-CEO Maurice Gallagher said: "Boeing was hungry, and our approach to fleet development has always been opportunistic." The order has since grown to 56 firm aircraft, and by the third quarter of 2026 the MAX accounted for 22% of Allegiant's available seat miles, up from 12% a year earlier. Its May 2026 acquisition of Sun Country Airlines added 43 Boeing 737-800s and three 737-900ERs to the combined group, which expects a single operating certificate in 2028.

facts.claim: Allegiant began operations in 1998 with McDonnell Douglas DC-9s and built a fleet of 61 MD-80s, 48 of them MD-83s, mostly built in the mid-to-late 1980s.

Allegiant began acquiring secondhand Airbus A319s and A320s from 2012; its January 2019 investor presentation put their fuel burn about 25-30% below the MD-80, and the final MD-80 passenger flight in November 2018 made it an all-Airbus operator.
On January 5, 2022, Allegiant ordered 50 Boeing 737 MAX aircraft, 30 737-7s and 20 737-8-200s, with options for 50 more; the order has since grown to 56 firm aircraft.

Allegiant completed its acquisition of Sun Country Airlines in May 2026; as of September 30, 2026, the combined group operated 76 A320s, 27 A319s, 21 737 MAX 8-200s, 43 737-800s and three 737-900ERs, and expects a single operating certificate in 2028.
